reason: The surface must lose heat before it can retain liquid water, so escaping infrared energy is a plausible starting point.
expectation: The lava and surrounding rock will cool as energy escapes.

effect: The cooler rock can retain liquid water, completing the surface-cooling goal; rain still needs to form.
reaction: The contrast between cool rock and nearby hot lava makes the uneven cooling clear.
reason: Cooler air above the steam-rich atmosphere should encourage water vapor to condense into clouds or rain.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

expectation: Water vapor will condense, beginning the formation of rain.

effect: Condensation formed clouds, but rain still needs to reach the ground.
reaction: The distinction between clouds and a surface sea is useful.
reason: Gravity should pull cloud droplets down as rain.
expectation: The droplets will fall as rain toward the surface.

effect: Cloud droplets are now falling as rain, but the rain-reaching-ground goal remains open.
reaction: It is interesting that falling rain can still evaporate before reaching the surface.
reason: The cooler rock can retain liquid water, making it the most promising surface for the falling rain.
expectation: Rain will reach the cooler rock and remain liquid there.

effect: Rain first reached hot lava and returned as steam; the cooler rock has not yet received it.
reaction: I was surprised the rain had to encounter the hot patch before the cool rock.
reason: The steam needs to cool and condense again before rain can reach the cooler surface, so I’ll check its available partners.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the steam returns to the rain cycle.

effect: The returned steam has no available combination, so I need another route to the rain goal.
reaction: I expected the steam to rejoin the rain cycle, so the empty partner list is surprising.
reason: The cool rock can retain water, so checking its available partners may reveal how to get rain onto it.
expectation: Inspection should reveal an available way to bring water to the cool rock.

effect: The cool rock has no available partner, so it cannot currently advance the rain goal.
reaction: The lack of a direct route to the cool rock is puzzling.
reason: The steam-rich atmosphere produced clouds before, and inspecting it may reveal whether another route is available.
expectation: The inspection will show its currently available partners, possibly including the cooler air.

effect: The atmosphere is cooling as energy escapes, revealing another step toward rain reaching the ground.
reaction: The coupled cooling of atmosphere and surface clarifies why cooling the rock alone was not enough.
reason: The cooled atmosphere is the new development, but its next partner is not yet clear.
expectation: Inspection will reveal how the cooling atmosphere can progress toward rain.

effect: The cooling atmosphere and returned steam now form water recycled through the sky, suggesting another chance for rain.
reaction: The steam’s role in the water cycle is clearer now.
reason: The recycled water is the latest development, but its next available partner is unclear.
expectation: Inspection will reveal how the recycled water can progress toward rain reaching the ground.

effect: Recycled water condensed in cooler air into persistent heavy rain, which can now be brought to the cooled surface.
reaction: The distinction between transient rain and rain that survives cooling is clearer.
reason: The cool rock can retain liquid water, making it a plausible destination for the persistent rain.
expectation: The rain will reach the cool rock and remain liquid there.

effect: Persistent rain remained liquid on the cool rock, completing the rain goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the rain finally stay on the ground after recycling through the atmosphere.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the steam atmosphere was the most worthwhile turn: it showed why the atmosphere and surface must lose heat together, not just the rock alone.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the returned steam and cool rock yielded no partners, making that stretch puzzling and unproductive until the atmosphere was checked.

surprise.text: I expected the falling rain to reach the cool rock directly, but it first hit hot lava and returned as steam; atmospheric cooling then enabled it to recycle.

arbitrary.text: Having to send rain to the hot lava before it could reach the cool rock felt somewhat forced, even though the resulting evaporation made physical sense.

continue.text: I would continue: the coupled cooling and recycled rain made me curious how water would accumulate into a larger body.
